issues.legal_issue: The presumption under Section 90 of the Evidence Act for documents more than thirty years old cannot, by itself, establish due execution and attestation of a will.
When no attesting witness to a will can be found, the will may be proved under Section 69 of the Evidence Act by proving the handwriting of the executor and of at least one attesting witness.

A will may be proved through other evidence when its attesting witnesses are unavailable, and the evidence in this case sufficiently established its due execution and the propounder’s entitlement to letters of administration.
